items.title: Cameras attached to whale sharks capture krill chases never witnessed before
items.summary: Whale sharks (Rhincodon typus)—the world's biggest fish—are one of the most charismatic marine species. They connect with the hearts of anyone lucky enough to encounter them, making people deeply curious about their lives and invested in their conservation.

items.title: China evacuates 340,000 people as Typhoon Noul approaches
items.summary: Authorities have evacuated more than 340,000 people and suspended work and rail services as Typhoon Noul approaches southern China, with flight cancellations announced in Hong Kong.

items.title: Spain fights to 'save lives' as wildfire evacuees shelter in Madrid
items.summary: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said Saturday firefighters were working to "save lives" in the blazes raging west of Madrid, as authorities said a separate fire in the east killed one person.

items.title: SpaceX launches Starship on another test flight, this time with the most advanced Starlinks
items.summary: SpaceX's mammoth Starship rocket blasted off Friday on another test flight stretching halfway around the world, this time releasing 20 of the most advanced Starlinks.

items.title: The hunt for a natural molecule that can release cellular energy
items.summary: All cells in the human body—and the motions they enable, from our beating hearts to our wiggling toes—use energy generated by a molecule called ATP. items.title: Ancient bones from smaller Maya communities reveal heavy reliance on maize and local subsistence patterns
items.summary: Historians and archaeologists know that maize was a central food source and cultural symbol across the ancient Maya world, but much of what is known has come from studies focused on large Maya cities and elite burials.

items.title: A single dose reversed autism-like symptoms in adult mice within hours
items.summary: Even mild inflammation during pregnancy led mouse offspring to develop persistent brain overactivity, sensory sensitivity, repetitive behaviors, and increased seizure risk. items.title: Herbivore species dynamics is key to grassland food web stability
items.summary: Ecologists have long understood that biodiversity is paramount to ecosystem stability. items.title: Superagers keep youthful memories but their DNA does not explain why
items.summary: Scientists expected SuperAgers might simply inherit fewer Alzheimer’s-related risks, but their genes looked much like those of typical older adults. Their extraordinary memories may instead come from still-unknown protective forces involving the brain, body, lifestyle, and environment.

items.title: Scientists put the “recycling is a distraction” claim to the test
items.summary: Recycling, greener diets, and other personal climate choices do not seem to distract people from supporting major environmental reforms. A four-year study of nearly 2,800 Australians found that these habits neither increased nor reduced later political engagement.

items.title: The Universe can outrun light without breaking Einstein’s rules
items.summary: Cosmic expansion allows distant galaxies to move away faster than light, while still letting us see ancient light they emitted when they were much closer. Eventually, accelerating expansion will push nearly every galaxy beyond our Local Group out of sight, making the Universe appear almost empty.

items.title: Rare blue optical transient points to possible new class of cosmic explosion
items.summary: Chinese astronomers report the detection of a peculiar optical transient event that occurred in the center of a dwarf galaxy. items.title: Oral GLP-1 drugs may quiet the brain’s food craving circuit
items.summary: Newer oral drugs related to semaglutide medications such as Ozempic reduced pleasure-driven eating in mice by quieting a deep brain reward circuit. The finding could open new avenues for understanding food cravings and potentially treating substance use disorder.

items.title: A daily fiber supplement reduced knee arthritis pain and improved strength
items.summary: A prebiotic fiber supplement reduced knee osteoarthritis pain while also improving grip strength and pain sensitivity in a six-week trial. The results hint at a fascinating gut-muscle-pain connection and suggest that a simple daily supplement may be easier to maintain than digital physiotherapy.

items.title: SpaceX-ov Starship uspješno dovršio ključni testni let
items.summary: SPACEX-OVA raketa Starship uspješno je dovršila 13. testni let. Potisnik i letjelica kontrolirano su sletjeli u ocean, a izbačeno je i 20 Starlink satelita. Ovo je važan korak za misiju na Mjesec.

items.title: Venus may be tearing itself apart from within
items.summary: Scientists have uncovered new evidence that Venus may still be tearing itself apart from within. items.summary: A new analysis suggests the Sun holds far more silver than earlier estimates indicated. items.title: Smarter, greener ways to protect fragile cultural heritage
items.summary: Museums, libraries, archives and heritage organizations face a difficult problem: Many of the objects they preserve are made from materials that naturally deteriorate.

items.title: Wound odors may unlock better traps for flesh-eating New World screwworm
items.summary: Jessica Metcalf's work stinks. Literally. But the Colorado State University professor's research may be key to protecting livestock and wildlife from a flesh-eating parasite.

items.summary: Nitrate contamination of drinking water poses a major health concern, particularly in agricultural communities where fertilizers, livestock manure and septic systems can leach nitrates into groundwater.
